## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Growth — discover local packs (per repo)

A weekly reflection on **this repo's own** captured knowledge: knowing the Claudinite packs already available to it, notice when project-specific knowledge is worth organizing into a **new local pack** — and author it. Finding nothing new worth a pack is a perfectly good, common outcome.

There is no windowed Context to bind — the opportunity is standing (knowledge that was never organized into a pack, not a recent change), so examine the repo as it is.

This run opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge**. Extract may land unreviewed because it adds prose or a rule to territory a local pack already owns; a **new pack** ships new `.mjs` conformance checks that run at every Stop and in CI the moment it merges — a check can break CI, so it's reviewed, exactly as the sibling [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md) is.

=== ci.yml ===
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so baselining can start this run on the nightly maintenance PR.
  # That PR's branch push and its open both ride the Action's GITHUB_TOKEN, and
  # GitHub's recursion guard suppresses workflow runs for events that token
  # authors — so the PR gets no pull_request run at all, and `maintenance.delivery:
  # auto-merge` waits on a check that never appears. workflow_dispatch is the
  # guard's one documented exception, which is why baselining's deliver() starts
  # the checks itself.
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Claudinite world-scope conformance sweep
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      # The glob is explicit on purpose: bare `node --test` skips dot-directories,
      # so it would find none of these and still exit green (claudinite-website/node-test-discovery).
      - name: Local pack rule fixtures
        run: node --test '.claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs'
=== deploy-pages.yml ===
# Publishes site/ to GitHub Pages on every push to main (no paths filter).
# Artifact-flow deploy (no gh-pages branch); the custom domain (claudinite.com)
# is configured in the repository's Pages settings, not here — see
# site/README.md. Uploading site/ (never the repo root) keeps the agent-tooling
# dirs out of the artifact.
name: Deploy site to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  # write: the release commits its version bump back to main
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Every production release advances the version. package.json is the single
      # source of truth; the bumped files are committed back to main so the number
      # in the repo always names the last release that actually went out. The
      # script also stamps the site's footer tooltip from that same number —
      # see scripts/bump-version.mjs.
      - name: Bump version
        id: bump
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION=$(node scripts/bump-version.mjs)
          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Released version $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Commit the version bump
        # [skip ci] keeps this commit from re-triggering this workflow, so there
        # is no deploy loop. Rebase-and-retry because the Claudinite scheduler and
        # its maintenance PRs also land on main, and a race here would otherwise
        # lose the bump and leave the repo claiming an older version than shipped.
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add package.json site/*.html
          git commit -m "Bump version to ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} [skip ci]"
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            if git push origin HEAD:main; then
              echo "Pushed the version bump on attempt $attempt."
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = "5" ]; then
              echo "Failed to push the version bump after $attempt attempts." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Push rejected — rebasing on latest main and retrying (attempt $attempt)."
            git pull --rebase origin main
          done
      - name: Inject Cloudflare Web Analytics token
        # The beacon token is public (it ships in the client), so it lives in a
        # repo *variable*, not a secret. When set, substitute it into the served
        # analytics.js; when unset, the placeholder stays and analytics no-ops.
        # sed uses '#' as its delimiter so the line contains no shell pipe.
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN" ]; then
            sed -i "s#REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN#${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN}#" site/assets/analytics.js
            echo "Injected Cloudflare Web Analytics token from the CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN variable."
          else
            echo "CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN variable not set — analytics stays off (placeholder retained)."
          fi
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
        with:
          # First run enables Pages (source: GitHub Actions) if the token is
          # allowed to; otherwise enable it once in Settings → Pages.
          enablement: true
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: site
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
